summary: Light regression smoke test after removal of `googleServicesFile` from /app/frontend/app.json. All 6 backend smoke tests pass (100%): GET /api/ (200 with correct payload), POST /api/auth/login admin (JWT returned), POST /api/register-push (returns 201 {status: pending, note: 'push key placeholder'} — non-500, contract preserved), POST /api/appointments (200, non-blocking push), POST /api/payments/create-order Razorpay (200 with order_id), POST /api/video/session Daily.co (200 with room url). Frontend web preview loads cleanly at http://localhost:3000 with 0 JS errors, landing screen renders (Online Vaidhyaji branding, Sign in visible). app.json is valid JSON, `expo-notifications` plugin still declared (local notifications + iOS push preserved), no dangling `googleServicesFile` reference. Confirmed google-services.json is not present in /app/frontend/ (as expected — the fix removes the reference until user provides the file). No regressions detected.
action_items: NONE — the one-line removal is safe. When user provides google-services.json, re-add `"googleServicesFile": "./google-services.json"` under `expo.android` in app.json to re-enable Android FCM push.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter 13 verified: the removal of `googleServicesFile` from app.json did not regress any backend endpoint or frontend load path. rca_of_issue: N/A — verification-only. The original EAS build blocker was caused by app.json referencing `./google-services.json` while the file did not exist. Removing that one line unblocks EAS PREBUILD. Local notifications and iOS push remain functional because the expo-notifications plugin is still declared. Android FCM will be re-enabled by adding the file + re-adding the app.json line.
